curated-gf-gochi-hand-roboto-slab: Gochi Hand crowds its lowercase up against the cap line, like a quick friendly scrawl. Roboto Slab steps in with open, structured slab-serif letters, and a heading this lively is best big and short (a general purpose flyer, say).
curated-gf-goldman-gf-montserrat-alterna: Commanding letters spread wide, with Goldman's round forms curving like open parentheses. Make that heading small and its generous spacing gets lost, while Montserrat Alternates, with its tube-like constant stroke and chalk-board lowercase, would feel heavy if blown up large.
curated-gf-gorditas-gf-poltawski-nowy: Fat, round and rope-spaced, Gorditas has no tilt in its curves at all. Poltawski Nowy brings a traditional, literary classic serif voice underneath, so the loud heading gets one quiet partner and the two never compete.
curated-gf-grand-hotel-gf-noto-serif-tc: Grand Hotel pairs tall verticals with small closed round letters, like a casual note with a lightly varying pen. Noto Serif TC holds its letters open in a classic serif, which makes it comfortable for a few lines.
curated-gf-grape-nuts-fs-spline-sans: Relaxed and friendly, Grape Nuts leaves its rounds unlatched. Spline Sans keeps its curves wide open and its strokes identical in weight, so the loose hand-drawn heading gets a steady partner (a woodworking shop sign, perhaps, though only in passing).
curated-gf-grape-nuts-gf-aoboshi-one: Aoboshi One, a text serif, leads the way here. Grape Nuts is the one for hand-drawn friendliness with tall l and k, while Aoboshi One handles classic, shrunken-looking lowercase, say, for an indie comic series logo.
curated-gf-grape-nuts-gf-google-sans-cod: Tall l and k tower over Grape Nuts' unlatched rounds, handy for, say, a classical recital poster. The heading is best at loose, friendly warmth, while Google Sans Code does the technical, measured beat of fixed-width monospace letters.
curated-gf-grape-nuts-gf-hahmlet: Grape Nuts draws its loose, friendly rounds at a single stroke width. Hahmlet adds a dignified, editorial serif with slight weight changes and a widely parted c and s, so the hand-drawn heading sits above something more formal.
curated-gf-gravitas-one-general-sans: Wide-open tracking and swollen curves that thin to wire-like ends set Gravitas One apart (handy on a team shirt for an event, say). General Sans is where the quiet work happens, with its sans-serif strokes drawn at one weight and an x-height that fills the line.
curated-gf-gravitas-one-gf-headland-one: Gravitas One swells its curves to commanding thick verticals and lets the hairlines recede. Headland One is the better text serif for a few lines, with well-spaced letters and a tall rounded o that nearly matches its capital.
